findings.summary: The --summary mode's whole risk is over-claiming: a dev-vs-holdout gap read off 2 plants is noise dressed as signal (the first real run was recall 2/2 with a Wilson interval of [0.34-1.00]). A naive comparison would have printed a scary/false 'below dev' verdict on nothing.
findings.disposition: holdout_summary_lines WITHHOLDS the comparison entirely when n<8 ('too small to compare; author more plants'), and only emits WATCH when holdout recall is materially (>=15 points) below dev WITH enough plants. It reuses history_format.interval_cell (Wilson) rather than a bare point estimate, so the reading itself carries its uncertainty. Tested three ways: small-n withholds, enough-plants-and-below-dev -> WATCH, and the reading shows the interval. Recorded incorporated (tests in the calibration harness, not suite_glob, per the RS-P2 constraint).

findings.summary: A --summary run reads the calibration history and the run's stdout to build its reading — both must stay answer-key-safe (no plant/oracle text).
findings.disposition: _filtered_run_lines keeps ONLY scenario headers (id+agent, which the egress allow-list already strips of plant text in holdout mode), verdict lines (runs/mode counts), and the Calibration reading — it drops everything else. holdout_summary_lines reads history rows, which carry ids + counts only (bodies never enter history, arch-F4). No oracle/plant text on the summary path.
